comment: I'm not sure if you also check for naturalness of the tip-of-tongue query (i.e. would an actual human ask such a query when trying to recall a paper), but in my opinion, the most distinctive thing about this paper is that it is about suicide ideation detection in a low resource language setting and the query focused on all the other details except that. If there is a judgement criteria on naturalness, I think this query would score pretty low. Just wanted to point that out!

it was slightly difficult to decide between partially relevant and highly relevant - while all the details were correct, many parts of the query generally apply to many papers (e.g. having an ablation analysis and comparing multiple methods on different datasets). In terms of the percentage score, I think this is about ~70%. In the end, I marked this as partially relevant as the key distinction of the paper to me is using negative sampling to degrade reference summaries but this was not mentioned explicitly. Although sentence transformations were mentioned, the context of why these transformations were made, which is to create negative samples, was not mentioned, so there was no clear link to the negative sampling mechanism. This made me think that this query could possibly apply to other papers on this topic that also use pairwise preference learning but use a different mechanism.
The details of the diagram in the query is wrong, but the other details on the mechanism is specific enough to identify this paper. This would be a low "Highly Relevant", around ~85%
